name: Bixaceae

lineage_context.teaching_goal: Teach Cochlospermum wrightii through its tuberous geophyte habit, palmately lobed leaves, showy 5-petaled yellow flowers with numerous free stamens and capsules full of woolly-haired seeds.

project_scope.note: Accepted current name; native range begins in southwest Texas and extends southward.

family_diagnostics.where_to_look_first: Start with the flower: five large yellow petals surround a dense mass of numerous free stamens rather than a mallow-style staminal column.
family_diagnostics.vegetative: Project plant is a tuberous geophyte/seasonal herb with alternate palmately lobed leaves and caducous stipules.
family_diagnostics.reproductive: Showy bisexual 5-merous flowers, free petals, numerous free stamens; superior ovary with many ovules.
family_diagnostics.fruit: Multi-valved capsule with many curved/reniform seeds clothed in long soft white hairs.
family_diagnostics.field_tip: Palmately lobed seasonal plant + huge yellow 5-petaled flower + many free stamens + woolly seeds = project Bixaceae/Cochlospermum.

visual_lesson.teaching_order: tuberous habit → palmately lobed leaf → giant yellow flower → free stamens → capsule → woolly seed → Malvaceae comparison
visual_lesson.intro: Yellowshow can look mallow-like from a distance, but the flower center and fruit settle it: the stamens stay free, and the capsule releases woolly seeds.

steps.title: 1 · Show the seasonal geophyte body plan
steps.look_for: Above-ground shoots arising from a persistent tuberous underground system.
steps.why_it_matters: Explains survival in seasonally dry habitat.

steps.title: 2 · Read the palmate leaf
steps.look_for: Deeply palmately lobed blade on a long petiole.

steps.title: 3 · Look into the yellow flower center
steps.look_for: Five broad yellow petals and many separate stamens.
steps.why_it_matters: Separates it from local Malvaceae's fused staminal column.

steps.title: 4 · Open the capsule
steps.look_for: Three- to five-valved dry capsule opening to expose many seeds.

steps.title: 5 · Zoom into a woolly seed
steps.look_for: Curved/reniform seed wrapped in fine long white hairs.
steps.why_it_matters: One of the best family/genus visual signatures.

comparisons.title: Bixaceae vs Malvaceae
comparisons.rule: Both can be showy and palmately veined, but project Cochlospermum has numerous free stamens and a woolly-seeded capsule; local Malvaceae commonly has stamens fused into a conspicuous central column.

visual_lesson.caveat: Do not use yellow flower + palmate leaf alone. The free stamens and woolly seeds make the project Bixaceae lesson reliable.

genera.fast_cue: tuberous geophyte + palmate leaf + giant yellow flower with many free stamens + woolly seeds

taxonomy_reconciliation.note: Accepted; native range includes southwest Texas.
Homotypic synonym retained as searchable provenance.
